records.our_prose: For a tree, 'companions' is really root-zone management, not vegetable pairing. The single most important rule is to keep lawn grass and weeds well clear of the root zone out to the drip line: turf competes hard for water and nitrogen and slows a young citrus markedly. Keep organic mulch pulled back at least a foot from the trunk to reduce Phytophthora foot-rot risk. Because lemon is self-fruitful, there is no need to site a second tree nearby for pollination. Low, shallow-rooted plantings outside the drip line are harmless; anything that crowds the trunk or holds moisture against it is not. (Sources: Texas A&M AgriLife, UF/IFAS.)

records.our_prose: Asymmetric blotchy yellow mottling that crosses leaf veins unevenly, yellow shoots, twig dieback, and small, lopsided, poorly colored fruit that stays partly green and tastes bitter, with seeds often aborted. Decline is progressive and the disease is ultimately fatal to the tree. It is the disease that has devastated the Florida citrus industry and is the reason home citrus growing declined there.
